text:
Cheng: heads-up — noticed APAC GPU nodepool didn't scale during the qps spike this morning, apps hit p99 latency.
Maria: same, SLO alerts fired at 08:12 UTC, I saw a bunch of pods Pending with `0/1 nodes available`.
Alex: do we have autoscaler events? CA logs show scale-up attempted then failed with a provisioning error.
ops-bot: [cluster-autoscaler] scale up: nodegroup=asia-gpu-pool, candidates=1, unneeded=false
Cheng: important bit — HPA was using our external latency metric; HPA increased replicas, but pods stayed Pending because GPU quota in the region was exhausted and new VMs were stuck in PROVISIONING.
Maria: right — cloud console showed NIC/egress quota error for the project in asia-southeast1. New nodes never joined.
Alex: ah, so CA requested nodes but cloud quota rejected them. CA marked attempt failed, then VPA kicked in and started recommending evictions to compact pods onto partial nodes.
Sam: VPA evicting GPU pods during scale-up? that's brutal. Eviction churn made more pods Pending because eviction timing overlapped with provisioning lag.
Cheng: here's the sequence I pieced together:
- HPA triggers replica increase (latency metric -> external-metric-p99)
- Cluster Autoscaler requests new gpu node
- Cloud provider returns quota error (NIC/EGRESS) -> node stuck PROVISIONING
- CA marks scale-up failed and backs off
- VPA (on) suggests eviction to rebalance; controller evicts a few pods
- Evictions cause other pods to become Pending and HPA ramps more replicas
- Feedback loop, higher cost/risk and user-visible p99 spikes
Maria: logs snippet from kube-event-collector:
```
Normal  FailedCreatePodSandBox  pod/gpu-infer-xyz Unable to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create network namespace: quota exceeded: NICs
Warning FailedScheduling pod/gpu-infer-abc 0/5 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu, 4 node(s) didn't match node affinity.
``` 
Alex: we've seen similar CA+HPA churn before but usually warm-pool masks it. Not this time because region quotas are sticky.
Sam: action items I propose:
- temporarily pause VPA for gpu workloads (annotation: "vpa.k8s.ai/enable: 'false'") to avoid eviction during provisioning blips
- add a preflight check in our scale policy to evaluate cloud quota before CA requests (or monitor quota and disable autoscale if near limit)
- adjust HPA to use a smoothed latency metric (longer stable-window) to avoid immediate replica spikes from transient tails
- add a CA scale-up fallback to try alternate region or burst pool (if configured)
Maria: +1 on VPA off for GPUs. Also we should have a runbook to top up regional quotas proactively. Cost vs availability tradeoff.
Cheng: minor tweak — HPA should set behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds to 120 or 180 for latency-based external metrics. We already do 30s for qps; latency needs longer.
Alex: can also add PodDisruptionBudget tweaks to prevent VPA from evicting too many pods at once: set maxUnavailable to 1 for critical gpu services.
Sam: I'm going to open a quick infra ticket to request NIC quota increase and also annotate the nodepool with `scale-protection=true` until quota confirmed.
Cheng: echo Sam — I'll also put a temporary alert that watches for CA scale-up failures with quota-related messages and pages infra-oncall.
ops-bot: [ticket] INFRA-3421 created by Sam: "APAC GPU quota increase & temporary VPA disable on GPU workloads" link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421
Maria: one more thought: for long-term, we should consider a soft-routing policy: if APAC capacity is low, route some batch-ish inference to eu-west burst pool automatically to preserve SLOs.
Alex: cost note — cross-region routing raises egress and higher tail latency; add to PRD so product agrees on cost vs availability.
Cheng: agreed. For now I'll add the VPA annotation to the gpu namespaces and extend HPA stabilization on the latency metric. Sam, please escalate quota request to cloud provider contacts.
Sam: will do, pinging vendor now. updating ticket with contact and ETA.
Maria: thanks all — posting a short postmortem draft in #incidents after we stabilize.
Cheng: thanks — keeping this thread as the action log. :thumbsup:
